name: Sega Saturn
description: Sega's 32-bit CD-ROM console, built around two Hitachi SH-2 processors and a pair of custom video chips. Strong in Japan and loved for 2D arcade ports, it struggled in the West against the PlayStation after a rushed surprise launch.

specs.memory: 2 MB RAM / 1.5 MB VRAM / 512 KB sound RAM

curiosities: Sega announced at the first E3 in May 1995 that the Saturn was already on sale in the US, months ahead of the planned date.
The Saturn draws 3D scenes with quadrilaterals rather than the triangles used by most 3D hardware.
Its CD copy protection was only fully bypassed in 2016, more than 20 years after launch.
A cartridge slot accepted RAM expansion carts that some Capcom and SNK fighting games required.
story: Sega designed the Saturn for 2D, with two Hitachi SH-2 processors, and added more 3D power late, when the PlayStation's plans became known. It launched in Japan in November 1994 and did well there.

In North America Sega launched it by surprise in May 1995, months early, angering shops; Sony then priced the PlayStation $100 lower. Hard to program, it lost the West, though Virtua Fighter 2, Nights into Dreams, Panzer Dragoon Saga and the arcade ports made it a cult machine.
It sold about nine million units, most in Japan, and Sega replaced it with the Dreamcast in 1998.
